newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine pension inspector shot by suspect's husband.
newsitem.headline: Argentine pension inspector shot by suspect's husband.

text.p: An Argentine social security inspector investigating a bribes-for-pensions racket was shot to death by the husband of a civil servant he was about to accuse of graft, local media reported on Thursday.

Witnesses said Alfredo Pochat, a 39-year-old Special Investigator for the social security service ANSSES in the city of Mar del Plata, was killed by the husband of ANSSES manager Silvia Andreo an hour before he was scheduled to hold a news conference naming her and four others.
Mar del Plata is on the Atlantic coast some 250 miles (400 kms) south of Buenos Aires.

Armando Andreo, whose wife Silvia was fired last month on suspicion of running a gang that awarded pensions in exchange for bribes, shot Pochat twice with a handgun at his office on Wednesday. He was arrested and charged with murder.

Labour Minister Armando Caro Figueroa said Pochat had "uncovered a network trafficking in pensions. We have reached the conclusion that she (Silvia Andreo) was directly responsible for this criminal behaviour."
